cards.title: Introduction to Deployment
cards.content:
Deployment is the process of making your Python application available to users or other systems in a production environment.

Unlike running on localhost:8000, a production server requires security, stability, scalability, and automated process management.

options.text: A cloud server or Platform as a Service (PaaS)

cards.title: WSGI and ASGI Servers
cards.content:
Standard Python web frameworks (like Flask or Django) run on development servers that cannot handle heavy production traffic.

We use production-grade application servers like Gunicorn (WSGI for synchronous apps) or Uvicorn (ASGI for asynchronous apps like FastAPI).

gunicorn myproject.wsgi:application --bind 0.0.0.0:8000

cards.title: Match Python Servers to Use Cases
Environment Variables & Security
cards.content:
Never hardcode secrets like database passwords or API keys in your Python code.

Use the python-dotenv package or environment variables configured in your operating system/cloud host.

import os
DATABASE_URL = os.getenv('DATABASE_URL')

cards.title: Containerization with Docker
cards.content:
Docker packages your Python application, its dependencies, and the exact Python runtime into a single container image.

FROM python:3.10-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
CMD ["python", "main.py"]

items: Choose a base Python image (FROM python:3.10)
Specify the command to run the app (CMD)

cards.title: CI/CD Pipelines
cards.content:
Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) automates testing and deployment.

Tools like GitHub Actions run your pytest test suite and automatically deploy to your server upon pushing to the main branch.

options.text: Commit debug=True and hardcoded passwords to public GitHub
